correctness.rationale: The objective equals N(tr((L+11^T/N)^(-1))-1) on connected support. The trace inverse is strictly convex (its second derivative in a nonzero symmetric direction is strictly positive), and the simple-graph Laplacian is injective in edge weights. The compact budget domain and blow-up at disconnection ensure existence; rescaling exhausts the budget. Uniqueness forces orbit invariance, not vice versa. The nonzero eigenvalues are x with multiplicity m-1, x+ry with multiplicity m(r-1), and Nx once. With t=(x+ry)/x>=1 the normalized objective is alpha*A+beta*D+beta*A*t+alpha*D/t, whose unique minimum is on the boundary if alpha<=0 or beta*A>=alpha*D, and otherwise at sqrt(alpha*D/(beta*A)). The identity A+D=mr² gives the stated threshold including equality. A second check at the uniform star gives derivative -2N/x² for any leaf-to-leaf edge and -(N-1)/x² for any spoke. The gradient per unit price thus gives the same threshold regardless of peripheral candidate edges whenever at least one such edge is available. The light-price optimum tends to m²Ara/B, giving the stated ratio and divergence for fixed m and increasing r.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks selected objectives, not optimality at all parameters; the proof establishes the latter.
If there are no peripheral candidate edges, the star is always optimal and a sharp transition is vacuous; the actual equal-clique family has r,m>=2.
